[[File:Josh Radke portrait.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Josh Radke.]]
'''Josh Radke''' was a Decipher-era [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]], listed as Red 84 from Terryville, Ct. The slot was retired after Decipher's SWCCG run.<ref name="sm-fan" /> He wrote TheForce.Net's Flashback Premiere interview with [[Chuck Kallenbach]], bylined as Red 84. By February 2005 he had been in charge of Star Wars CCG content for TheForce.Net since the summer of 2000.<ref name="tfn-dgamer">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Star_Wars_CCG_Covered_in_New_Decipher_Online_Magazine_89921.asp Star Wars CCG Covered in New Decipher Online Magazine], TheForce.Net (28 February 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050308013433/http://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Star_Wars_CCG_Covered_in_New_Decipher_Online_Magazine_89921.asp Internet Archive]</ref> He edited and published ''[[dGamer]]'', an independent online magazine for [[Decipher]] gamers whose first issue was dated January/February 2005.<ref name="dgamer-fp">[http://dgamer.red84.com/ dGamer - A Magazine for DECIPHER Gamers], dgamer.red84.com (23 February 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050223115202/http://dgamer.red84.com/ Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="tfn-dgamer" /><ref name="pc-dl10-08">[http://www.swccgpc.com/downloads/category.php?id=10 Downloads: Player Articles and Newsletters], swccgpc.com (13 October 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081013105749/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/downloads/category.php?id=10 Internet Archive]</ref>

Decipher recruited volunteer Squadron Members in the 1990s to promote SWCCG locally (tournaments, demos, player support).

== Players Committee ==

On 2 December 2002, as Player Relations Advocate, Radke asked tournament directors to run holiday tournaments that would help those less fortunate, for example with a new, unopened toy or canned goods as the entry fee.<ref name="pc-dec02">[http://www.swccgpc.com/Archives/december02archives.htm December Updates], swccgpc.com (2 December 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030423221911/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/december02archives.htm Internet Archive]</ref> In April 2003 he wrote articles for ''[[Scrye]]'' magazine on the Players Committee's latest activities and on its upcoming virtual sets.<ref name="pc-apr03">[http://www.swccgpc.com/Archives/april03archives.htm April Updates], swccgpc.com (8 and 20 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030810085606/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/april03archives.htm Internet Archive]</ref> On 18 June 2003 he announced Decipher's $5,000 cash gift to the Players Committee, signing as SWCCG Player Advocate – Marketing.<ref name="pc-donation03">[http://www.swccgpc.com/News/decipherdonation06182003.htm Decipher Grants Monetary Gift to PC], swccgpc.com (18 June 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030809101827/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/decipherdonation06182003.htm Internet Archive]</ref> On 8 August 2003 he announced Rules Advocate [[Greg Anderson]]'s 90-minute rules Q&A of 14 August 2003 on Decipher's Star Wars Gameplay message board, held ahead of the [[2003 World Championship]].<ref name="pcf-2024-31434">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=31434#31434 SWCCG Rules Q&A with PC Rules Advocate Greg Anderson], Josh Radke, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (8 August 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040126045108/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=2024%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> Working with the Tournaments Department, he proposed on 9 November 2003 a series of Players Committee Invitationals for 2004: a Battle of Naboo in the United Kingdom, a Coruscant Invitational in New York City, a Bespin Invitational in Minnesota or Chicago and a Battle of Endor in Seattle, with an Alderaan Invitational and a Mon Calamari Invitational in Australia also considered. Players would need a rating of 1650 or more or a first or second place at another Players Committee championship tournament that year; entry fees would be $10–20, and prizes would include cash, collectibles and Day 2 byes.<ref name="pcf-2355-35763">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=35763#35763 Invitationals Poll], Josh Radke, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (9 November 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040323102043/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=2355%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> [[Brandon Schele]] wrote in October 2004 that the Invitationals of the 2004 circuit had never been held.<ref name="pcf-4042-55081">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=55081#55081 Worlds 2005], Brandon Schele, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (13 October 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041031162316/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=55081%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> [[Steve Florent]] wrote in November 2003 that Radke occasionally wrote articles about the game for ''[[Scrye]]'', which were usually posted on the Players Committee website soon after the magazine came out.<ref name="pcf-2475-37805">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=37805#37805 SWCCG Magazine?], Steve Florent, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (30 November 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040131223356/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=37815%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In December 2003 Radke recalled producing ''Starfire's Rebel Log'', a newsletter that thrived while it had steady contributors and faded after a few issues, and offered to revive it as a bi-monthly Players Committee publication if enough committed writers came forward.<ref name="pcf-2475-38944">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=38944#38944 SWCCG Magazine?], Josh Radke, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (27 December 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040131223356/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=37815%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>
